The findings confirm that ET-driven scheduling is both technically feasible and economically advantageous for sugar beet production on chernozem, and provide locally calibrated Kc values that can be adopted directly by advisory services operating in the region.

SYN-PUB-07491.title: Low-cost capacitive soil moisture probes: calibration across soil types
SYN-PUB-07491.text:
Low-cost capacitive soil moisture probes: calibration across soil types (2021, journal, Sensors in Agronomy).
Authors: Nenad Ilić (R0662); Tatjana Krstović (outside co-author); Aleksandar Petrović (outside co-author).
Capacitive soil moisture sensors offer a low-cost alternative to time-domain reflectometry (TDR) probes for continuous soil water monitoring, but their accuracy is strongly dependent on soil-specific calibration. This paper presents a systematic calibration procedure applied to a prototype capacitive probe across five soil types commonly encountered in Vojvodina: chernozem, humogley, sandy loam, silty clay loam, and saline solonetz. Laboratory calibration curves were developed by measuring probe output voltage against gravimetrically determined volumetric water content (VWC) across a range from air-dry to field saturation. Separate polynomial regression models were fitted for each soil type, and their coefficients of determination (R²) ranged from 0.94 to 0.98. Field validation was performed by co-locating calibrated capacitive probes with TDR probes in irrigated maize and sunflower plots. Mean absolute error across all soil types was below 0.024 m³ m⁻³, which is sufficient for practical irrigation scheduling applications. The study also assessed probe performance at three installation depths (15, 35, and 60 cm), confirming that calibration coefficients must be depth-specific in stratified soil profiles. The calibration methodology described here is directly applicable to the multi-depth probe array described in the authors' associated patent.

SYN-PUB-07492.title: Deficit irrigation of vegetables in a changing climate
SYN-PUB-07492.text:
Deficit irrigation of vegetables in a changing climate (2020, conference, Conference on Sustainable Field Crops).
Authors: Dragana Simić (outside co-author); Nenad Ilić (R0662); Jovana Marković (outside co-author).
Deficit irrigation—deliberate application of water below full crop evapotranspiration demand—is increasingly proposed as a strategy for adapting vegetable production to reduced water availability under climate change scenarios. This conference paper synthesises three years of field trial data from pepper, tomato, and courgette crops grown under regulated deficit irrigation (RDI) in an open-field system in northern Serbia. Treatments ranged from 100% ET replacement (full irrigation) to 50% ET replacement applied at different phenological stages. Yield, water use efficiency (WUE), and selected quality parameters were measured for each combination. Results indicated that mild deficit (70–80% ET) applied during vegetative growth stages did not significantly reduce marketable yield of pepper or courgette, whereas tomato showed greater sensitivity, particularly during fruit set. WUE improved by up to 31% under the best-performing deficit regime relative to full irrigation. Climate projections for the Pannonian Plain suggest that summer precipitation deficits will intensify, making deficit irrigation protocols an essential component of future farm adaptation strategies. Practical guidelines for deficit scheduling using inexpensive sensor-based feedback are proposed.

SYN-PUB-07493.title: A smartphone-based decision support application for real-time irrigation scheduling in smallholder vegetable production
SYN-PUB-07493.text:
A smartphone-based decision support application for real-time irrigation scheduling in smallholder vegetable production (2022, journal, Computers and Electronics in Agriculture Reports).
Authors: Nenad Ilić (R0662); Tatjana Krstović (outside co-author); Branislav Ostojić (outside co-author); Mirjana Dobričević (outside co-author).
Keywords: decision support system; irrigation scheduling; smartphone application; smallholder; Penman–Monteith.
Smallholder vegetable growers frequently lack access to reliable, timely irrigation advice, resulting in both over- and under-irrigation with associated yield and water losses. This paper describes the design, implementation, and on-farm evaluation of IrriAdvisor, a smartphone application that delivers real-time irrigation recommendations based on a combined ET-model and soil moisture feedback loop. The application retrieves daily meteorological data from a national weather service API and calculates crop-specific water demand using locally calibrated Penman–Monteith equations. Users can supplement model outputs with readings from low-cost capacitive soil moisture probes connected via Bluetooth to the mobile device. Recommendations are expressed as practical irrigation volumes and timing windows. Field evaluation was conducted across 14 smallholder farms in Vojvodina growing pepper, onion, and cucumber over a single growing season. Farmers using IrriAdvisor reduced water application by 21% on average compared with a control group, while marketable yields were statistically equivalent or higher. User acceptance surveys indicated high satisfaction with interface simplicity and notification reliability. The application architecture is described in sufficient detail to support replication and adaptation in other semi-arid regions with comparable data infrastructure.

SYN-PUB-07494.title: Drip versus furrow irrigation of processing tomato: water productivity, yield components, and soil water distribution
SYN-PUB-07494.text:
Drip versus furrow irrigation of processing tomato: water productivity, yield components, and soil water distribution (2022, journal, Irrigation and Drainage Science).
Authors: Nenad Ilić (R0662); Slobodan Vuković (outside co-author); Dragana Simić (outside co-author).
Keywords: drip irrigation; furrow irrigation; processing tomato; water productivity; soil water distribution.
Processing tomato is an economically significant crop in Vojvodina, yet comparative data on drip and furrow irrigation systems under local edaphoclimatic conditions remain limited. A two-season field experiment compared subsurface drip irrigation (SDI), surface drip irrigation (DI), and furrow irrigation (FI) at two water supply levels (100% and 80% ET replacement) on a chernozem soil. Soil water distribution was mapped weekly using a multi-depth capacitive probe array installed at representative locations within each treatment. Yield components—fruit number per plant, average fruit weight, and total marketable yield—as well as lycopene content and dry matter were measured at harvest. SDI achieved the highest water productivity (8.4 kg m⁻³) and uniform soil water distribution, while FI showed the highest deep percolation losses estimated from soil water balance calculations. Under the 80% ET treatment, SDI yield was not significantly different from full-irrigation SDI, suggesting strong potential for deficit management with this system. Energy requirements for pumping were also assessed and found to favour surface DI for small farm units. The results support a transition from furrow to drip systems as a water-saving strategy for the processing tomato sector.

SYN-PUB-07495.title: Calibration and long-term stability of a multi-depth capacitive soil moisture probe array under field conditions
SYN-PUB-07495.text:
Calibration and long-term stability of a multi-depth capacitive soil moisture probe array under field conditions (2023, journal, Biosystems Engineering).
Authors: Nenad Ilić (R0662); Tatjana Krstović (outside co-author); Aleksandar Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: soil moisture sensor; sensor drift; capacitive probe; field calibration; long-term stability.
The long-term reliability of capacitive soil moisture probes is a critical concern for continuous irrigation monitoring systems. This paper reports an 18-month field stability assessment of the capacitive multi-depth probe array described in patent SYN-PAT-001, installed in a chernozem profile under irrigated sugar beet and winter wheat rotation. Probe output was compared monthly against gravimetric sampling at corresponding depths (15, 35, and 60 cm). Drift in probe response was quantified using a linear drift model fitted to paired datasets, and a simple field recalibration procedure requiring only three gravimetric reference measurements was developed and tested. Drift rates were below 0.003 m³ m⁻³ per month at the 15 and 35 cm depths, but reached 0.007 m³ m⁻³ per month at 60 cm, attributed to seasonal shrink-swell cycles in the subsoil. Temperature compensation using a co-located thermistor reduced residual drift by 62%. The recalibration procedure restored mean absolute error to below 0.020 m³ m⁻³ at all depths. These results demonstrate that the probe array is suitable for multi-season deployment with periodic recalibration and inform recommended maintenance protocols for commercial deployment of the sensor system.

SYN-PUB-07496.title: Towards IoT-enabled irrigation management: integration of wireless soil moisture sensor networks with cloud-based decision support
SYN-PUB-07496.text:
Towards IoT-enabled irrigation management: integration of wireless soil moisture sensor networks with cloud-based decision support (2024, journal, Smart Agricultural Technology).
Authors: Nenad Ilić (R0662); Branislav Ostojić (outside co-author); Mirjana Dobričević (outside co-author); Lazar Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: IoT; LoRaWAN; irrigation automation; soil moisture sensor network; cloud decision support.
The proliferation of low-cost wireless sensor nodes and cloud computing platforms creates new opportunities for scalable, automated irrigation management at the farm level. This paper presents an architecture for integrating a network of capacitive soil moisture sensor nodes with a cloud-based irrigation decision support engine. Each node transmits volumetric water content readings at configurable intervals over a LoRaWAN protocol to a gateway, from which data are forwarded to a cloud platform for storage, visualisation, and scheduling computation. The scheduling engine combines incoming sensor data with ET₀ forecasts derived from a regional numerical weather prediction model to issue valve-control commands to a drip irrigation controller via MQTT messaging. The system was deployed at a 4-hectare experimental plot at the Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, and operated continuously for one full growing season of sugar beet. Automated scheduling reduced irrigation labour time by approximately 85% compared with manual sensor reading and scheduling. Water savings of 17% were achieved relative to a sensor-monitored manual scheduling control. Latency, packet loss, and battery consumption of sensor nodes are characterised, and design recommendations for scaling the architecture to larger farms are discussed.

SYN-PUB-07497.title: Crop coefficient determination for sugar beet under drip irrigation in the Pannonian Plain
SYN-PUB-07497.text:
Crop coefficient determination for sugar beet under drip irrigation in the Pannonian Plain (2021, journal, Agricultural Water Management).
Authors: Nenad Ilić (R0662); Slobodan Vuković (outside co-author); Jovana Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: crop coefficient; sugar beet; evapotranspiration; FAO-56; drip irrigation.
Locally determined crop coefficients (Kc) are essential inputs for evapotranspiration-based irrigation scheduling, yet published FAO-56 values may not adequately represent cultivar performance and micro-climate in the Pannonian Plain. This study determined single and dual crop coefficients for four commercially grown sugar beet cultivars under drip-irrigated conditions across two experimental sites on chernozem in Vojvodina. Actual crop evapotranspiration (ETc) was measured using a soil water balance approach supported by continuous multi-depth soil moisture monitoring. Reference ET₀ was calculated from an automatic weather station. Kc values were derived for four growth stages: initial, development, mid-season, and late season. The locally determined mid-season Kc ranged from 1.17 to 1.23 across cultivars, exceeding the FAO-56 tabulated value of 1.05 by 11–17%. Using locally derived Kc values in the scheduling algorithm reduced irrigation over-application by 14% without yield penalty. The dual Kc approach, separating basal crop and soil evaporation components, provided additional accuracy during canopy development phases. A simple lookup table of locally calibrated Kc values by growth stage and cultivar group is provided for immediate use by agricultural advisors.

SYN-PUB-07498.title: Effects of regulated deficit irrigation at critical growth stages on sunflower yield and oil content in semi-arid conditions
SYN-PUB-07498.text:
Effects of regulated deficit irrigation at critical growth stages on sunflower yield and oil content in semi-arid conditions (2020, journal, Field Crops Research).
Authors: Dragana Simić (outside co-author); Nenad Ilić (R0662); Mirjana Dobričević (outside co-author).
Keywords: sunflower; deficit irrigation; regulated deficit irrigation; oil content; water use efficiency.
Sunflower is among the most drought-tolerant field crops cultivated in Vojvodina, yet supplemental irrigation during critical growth stages can substantially improve both yield and oil content. This paper investigates the effects of regulated deficit irrigation (RDI) applied selectively at four growth stages—vegetative, bud formation, flowering, and grain filling—on yield components and seed oil content of a mid-maturity sunflower hybrid. A split-plot factorial experiment was conducted over three growing seasons at an experimental station near Zrenjanin. Deficit levels of 100%, 75%, and 50% ET replacement were applied at each stage, while other stages received full irrigation. Water use efficiency and oil yield per unit area were used as primary performance indices. Deficit irrigation at the vegetative stage had the smallest yield penalty, while deficit at flowering caused a 19–27% reduction in achene yield regardless of the water level tested. Oil content showed greater resilience, declining significantly only under the most severe deficit at flowering. The study concludes that sunflower irrigation strategies should protect the flowering stage and may safely reduce water application during vegetative growth, providing practical guidance for farmers facing water allocation constraints.

SYN-PUB-07499.title: Precision irrigation in field crops: a review of sensor-based feedback systems and decision support frameworks applicable to Vojvodina
SYN-PUB-07499.text:
Precision irrigation in field crops: a review of sensor-based feedback systems and decision support frameworks applicable to Vojvodina (2023, journal, European Journal of Agronomy Reviews).
Authors: Nenad Ilić (R0662); Tatjana Krstović (outside co-author); Aleksandar Petrović (outside co-author); Jovana Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: precision irrigation; soil moisture sensors; decision support systems; review; Vojvodina.
Precision irrigation represents a convergence of sensor technology, data analytics, and agronomy aimed at delivering the right amount of water to the right location at the right time. This review systematically examines published sensor-based feedback systems and decision support frameworks for field crop irrigation, with a focus on applicability to the Pannonian Plain agro-ecological context. Technologies reviewed include capacitive and TDR soil moisture sensors, electromagnetic induction soil mapping, UAV-mounted thermal cameras for crop water stress indices, and lysimeter-based evapotranspiration measurement. Decision support frameworks are evaluated across three categories: threshold-based scheduling, model-driven scheduling, and machine learning-assisted forecasting. Strengths and limitations of each approach are assessed in terms of data requirements, cost, scalability, and suitability for smallholder versus large commercial operations. A gap analysis identifies the limited availability of locally validated crop coefficient databases and the absence of standardised sensor calibration protocols for Vojvodina's diverse soil types as key barriers to adoption. The review concludes with a research agenda prioritising low-cost IoT sensor integration, open-access scheduling tools, and participatory co-design with farmers and advisory services.

SYN-PUB-08409.title: Early-season maize yield prediction from Sentinel-2 time series at parcel level
SYN-PUB-08409.text:
Early-season maize yield prediction from Sentinel-2 time series at parcel level (2024, journal, Journal of Applied Earth Observation in Agriculture).
Authors: Milica Stanković (R0765); Dragan Petković (outside co-author); Sonja Vukić (outside co-author); Lars Meinhardt (outside co-author).
Accurate early-season prediction of maize yield is critical for guiding agronomic decisions and regional food-security planning. This study presents a machine learning framework that ingests dense Sentinel-2 time-series data collected from early April through late June to generate parcel-level yield forecasts across 1,200 fields in the Vojvodina region of northern Serbia. Vegetation indices derived from ten spectral bands, including NDVI, EVI, and red-edge chlorophyll index, were computed at five-day intervals and used as input features to a gradient-boosted tree ensemble. Phenological curve fitting was applied to handle cloud-contaminated observations, retaining 87 % of parcels without manual gap-filling. Cross-validation on independent parcels yielded an RMSE of 0.41 t/ha and an R² of 0.83. Importantly, forecast skill was already statistically significant six weeks before anthesis, giving farmers and agricultural insurers a meaningful planning window. Sensitivity analysis showed that red-edge band combinations contributed most to prediction accuracy, outperforming traditional broadband indices. The approach was validated against official municipal yield statistics, confirming its scalability from field to regional scale. These findings support operational integration of Sentinel-2 time series into national crop-monitoring systems.

SYN-PUB-08410.title: Hyperspectral indices for nitrogen stress in winter wheat under variable irrigation
SYN-PUB-08410.text:
Hyperspectral indices for nitrogen stress in winter wheat under variable irrigation (2023, journal, Precision Farming Letters).
Authors: Milica Stanković (R0765); Tamara Ilić (outside co-author); Nikola Đorđević (outside co-author); Petra Varga (outside co-author).
Nitrogen stress is a primary limiter of winter wheat productivity, yet its early detection remains challenging with broadband multispectral sensors. This study evaluates a set of hyperspectral indices computed from airborne imaging spectroscopy data acquired over experimental plots in Vojvodina subjected to four irrigation regimes and three nitrogen application rates. Fifteen candidate indices spanning the visible, red-edge, and short-wave infrared regions were assessed for their sensitivity to leaf nitrogen concentration measured destructively at tillering, stem elongation, and heading stages. Results showed that indices combining reflectance near 705 nm and 750 nm consistently outperformed chlorophyll-based broadband proxies, especially under moderate water deficit conditions where the interaction between nitrogen and water stress confounds standard NDVI-based estimates. A partial least squares regression model trained on the full hyperspectral dataset achieved a cross-validated RMSE of 1.8 g N kg⁻¹ dry mass. Critically, model performance degraded only modestly when inputs were resampled to the spectral resolution of the upcoming HyperSERB spaceborne instrument, suggesting a viable path to operational mapping. These results have direct implications for variable-rate nitrogen management in precision farming systems.

SYN-PUB-08411.title: Fusing radar and optical imagery for soil moisture mapping in the Pannonian plain
SYN-PUB-08411.text:
Fusing radar and optical imagery for soil moisture mapping in the Pannonian plain (2022, conference, International Symposium on Agricultural Remote Sensing).
Authors: Milica Stanković (R0765); Uroš Marković (outside co-author); Zoltán Fehér (outside co-author); Claudia Reiter (outside co-author).
Mapping soil moisture at high spatial resolution over large agricultural areas requires the complementary strengths of synthetic aperture radar and optical Earth observation. This paper presents a data-fusion workflow that combines Sentinel-1 C-band backscatter with Sentinel-2 surface reflectance to estimate volumetric soil moisture content across the Pannonian plain. The approach uses a change-detection algorithm applied to multi-temporal Sentinel-1 imagery to isolate the soil moisture signal from vegetation and surface roughness contributions, with Sentinel-2 derived vegetation indices used to constrain the vegetation correction. Validation against a network of 24 in-situ TDR sensors distributed across arable fields in Serbia and Hungary showed a root-mean-square error of 0.034 m³/m³ and a correlation coefficient of 0.79. Spatial patterns were consistent with topographic wetness index maps and irrigation scheduling records. The ten-metre fusion product outperformed standalone radar retrievals, particularly during the growing season when canopy effects are strongest. Operational daily latency of the processing chain was demonstrated using cloud-based infrastructure, making the product suitable for near-real-time agricultural advisory services.

SYN-PUB-08412.title: Transfer learning for crop type maps when labels are scarce
SYN-PUB-08412.text:
Transfer learning for crop type maps when labels are scarce (2021, journal, Remote Sensing Methods).
Authors: Bojana Filipović (outside co-author); Milica Stanković (R0765); Mihajlo Lazić (outside co-author); Andrej Kovač (outside co-author).
Supervised crop type mapping with satellite imagery typically requires large quantities of geolocated field labels, a resource that is costly and temporally limited. This paper investigates the application of transfer learning to reduce label requirements for crop type classification in data-scarce target regions using multi-temporal Sentinel-2 imagery. A convolutional neural network pre-trained on a densely labelled source domain in central Hungary is fine-tuned with progressively smaller labelled subsets drawn from a target domain in northern Serbia. Classification accuracy for the six dominant crop types plateaued at a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.81 when only 5 % of the original target labels were used, compared to 0.76 achieved by a baseline random forest trained from scratch on the same reduced set. Domain adaptation was further improved by a novel spectral normalisation step that accounts for inter-regional differences in atmospheric correction residuals. Experiments with simulated label scarcity down to 50 labelled parcels demonstrate that the transfer approach remains viable even under extreme data poverty. The method generalises across two growing seasons, indicating robustness to phenological variability. These results offer a practical solution for extending crop mapping services into regions where systematic ground-truth collection programmes do not yet exist.

SYN-PUB-08413.title: Sentinel-2 phenological metrics as predictors of sunflower oil content in Vojvodina
SYN-PUB-08413.text:
Sentinel-2 phenological metrics as predictors of sunflower oil content in Vojvodina (2024, journal, European Journal of Agronomy and Remote Sensing).
Authors: Dragan Petković (outside co-author); Milica Stanković (R0765); Ana Veselinović (outside co-author); Markus Brenner (outside co-author).
Keywords: sunflower; oil content; phenology metrics; Sentinel-2; random forest; Vojvodina.
Sunflower is a dominant oilseed crop in the Vojvodina region of Serbia, yet remote sensing-based prediction of grain quality traits such as oil content remains largely unexplored. This study examines whether land surface phenology metrics extracted from dense Sentinel-2 time series can serve as meaningful predictors of harvest-time oil content measured in a multi-year field trial dataset spanning 340 parcels. Seven phenological indicators—including the timing of maximum NDVI, the integrated growing season NDVI, and the rate of senescence-phase greenness decline—were derived using a double-logistic fitting procedure. A random forest regression model trained on these features achieved a leave-one-season-out RMSE of 1.9 percentage points for oil content and an R² of 0.71. Feature importance analysis highlighted the senescence rate and the timing of peak red-edge reflectance as the most informative predictors, consistent with physiological understanding of lipid accumulation dynamics. The model was also tested on an independent hold-out region in southern Banat, where performance degraded only marginally. These results suggest that Sentinel-2 phenological metrics can complement traditional crop scouting for quality-oriented precision management and downstream contract pricing in the oilseed value chain.

SYN-PUB-08414.title: Automated parcel boundary delineation from multi-temporal Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery using graph-cut segmentation
SYN-PUB-08414.text:
Automated parcel boundary delineation from multi-temporal Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery using graph-cut segmentation (2023, journal, ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Earth Observation).
Authors: Mihajlo Lazić (outside co-author); Milica Stanković (R0765); Uroš Marković (outside co-author); Giulia Tonetti (outside co-author).
Keywords: parcel delineation; graph-cut segmentation; Sentinel-1; multi-temporal fusion; cadastral update.
Accurate and up-to-date agricultural parcel boundaries are a fundamental prerequisite for precision agriculture services, subsidy administration, and crop area statistics. Existing cadastral datasets in the Western Balkans are often outdated or geometrically inconsistent with current land use, motivating automated boundary delineation directly from satellite imagery. This paper presents an end-to-end pipeline that fuses multi-temporal Sentinel-1 SAR coherence and Sentinel-2 NDVI stacks within a graph-cut segmentation framework to delineate parcel boundaries at ten-metre resolution. The method exploits the temporal contrast between crop rotation patterns in neighbouring parcels rather than relying solely on single-date spectral differences, making it robust to within-field heterogeneity. Evaluation against a manually digitised reference dataset of 4,800 parcels in Vojvodina yielded a boundary F1 score of 0.84 and a mean parcel area error of 3.2 %. Performance was superior to both single-date optical segmentation and standalone SAR-based methods. The automated boundaries proved sufficient for downstream crop type classification, reducing label mismatch errors by 18 % compared to cadastral polygon inputs. The pipeline is fully cloud-compatible and processes a 1,000 km² tile in under 20 minutes, demonstrating operational scalability.

SYN-PUB-08415.title: Assessing drought stress in soybean using UAV-borne hyperspectral imaging and machine learning
SYN-PUB-08415.text:
Assessing drought stress in soybean using UAV-borne hyperspectral imaging and machine learning (2023, journal, Biosystems Engineering).
Authors: Milica Stanković (R0765); Tamara Ilić (outside co-author); Jovana Rančić (outside co-author); Stephan Hübner (outside co-author).
Keywords: drought stress; soybean; UAV hyperspectral; support vector regression; canopy water content.
Drought stress in soybean causes significant yield penalties in continental climates such as that of the Pannonian plain, and its early detection is essential for timely irrigation triggering. This study presents a workflow combining UAV-borne hyperspectral imaging at five-centimetre ground sampling distance with supervised machine learning to map canopy water stress indices at the within-field scale. Imagery was acquired weekly over a 14-week growing season at an experimental station near Rimski Šančevi, Serbia, under four controlled deficit irrigation treatments. A support vector regression model trained on hyperspectral features selected by recursive feature elimination achieved a cross-validated R² of 0.87 for leaf relative water content and 0.82 for stomatal conductance estimated from concurrent porometry measurements. Short-wave infrared bands between 1,380 and 1,480 nm and the water absorption feature near 970 nm were the most discriminative spectral regions. Temporal trajectories of stress severity aligned well with volumetric soil moisture profiles from buried sensors, providing independent validation. Upscaling experiments demonstrated that the UAV-derived stress maps retained 74 % of their information content when resampled to the spatial resolution of simulated HyperSERB data, underpinning the relevance of the approach for future operational spaceborne monitoring.

SYN-PUB-08416.title: Long-term trends in crop calendars across Vojvodina inferred from a 20-year Landsat time series
SYN-PUB-08416.text:
Long-term trends in crop calendars across Vojvodina inferred from a 20-year Landsat time series (2022, journal, Agricultural and Forest Meteorology).
Authors: Milica Stanković (R0765); Sonja Vukić (outside co-author); Lars Meinhardt (outside co-author); Aleksandar Simić (outside co-author).
Keywords: phenology trends; Landsat time series; climate change; Vojvodina; crop calendar.
Understanding how crop phenology has shifted in response to climate change is essential for adaptive agricultural management in the Pannonian region. This study reconstructs 20-year trends in planting, peak growth, and harvest dates for the four dominant arable crops—maize, winter wheat, sunflower, and sugar beet—across Vojvodina, using a harmonised Landsat 5, 7, and 8 surface reflectance archive from 2000 to 2020. A robust double-logistic curve was fitted pixel-wise to annual NDVI trajectories, and phenological transition dates were derived at the parcel level using field-boundary polygons digitised from topographic maps. Statistically significant trends were found for all four crops: maize silking advanced by an average of 6.3 days per decade, while winter wheat heading advanced by 4.1 days per decade. These shifts correlated strongly with April–May temperature anomalies derived from regional gridded climate reanalysis data. Sugar beet exhibited the smallest phenological shifts, consistent with its flexible sowing window. Spatial heterogeneity in trend magnitude was partly explained by soil texture, with lighter sandy soils showing earlier and more pronounced advancement. These findings provide an empirical baseline for calibrating crop growth models under future climate scenarios and for redesigning crop rotation strategies in the region.

SYN-PUB-08417.title: Semi-supervised contrastive learning for crop stress detection from satellite imagery with limited annotations
SYN-PUB-08417.text:
Semi-supervised contrastive learning for crop stress detection from satellite imagery with limited annotations (2024, journal, IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing).
Authors: Milica Stanković (R0765); Bojana Filipović (outside co-author); Nikola Đorđević (outside co-author); Rolf Steinmann (outside co-author).
Keywords: contrastive learning; semi-supervised; crop stress detection; temporal transformer; Sentinel-2.
Labelling crop stress events in satellite image time series is labour-intensive, as it requires field validation campaigns that are both costly and weather-dependent. This paper introduces a semi-supervised learning framework based on contrastive pre-training to detect multiple stress categories—drought, nutrient deficiency, and waterlogging—from Sentinel-2 multi-temporal imagery using a fraction of labelled examples. The model pre-trains a temporal transformer encoder on 800,000 unlabelled parcel time series from four Vojvodina counties by maximising agreement between augmented views of the same parcel. Fine-tuning with as few as 200 labelled stress events per class yields a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.77, compared to 0.61 for a fully supervised baseline trained on the same labelled subset. Ablation studies confirm that both the temporal attention mechanism and the augmentation strategy—which applies random cloud masking and band dropout—are critical to performance. The framework also generalises to an unseen Hungarian test region with minimal performance loss after five-shot domain adaptation. By dramatically reducing annotation requirements, this approach makes satellite-based crop stress monitoring accessible to national agricultural advisory services with limited resources for systematic field data collection.

SYN-PUB-08418.title: Remote sensing-based estimation of above-ground biomass in heterogeneous arable fields: a comparative benchmark
SYN-PUB-08418.text:
Remote sensing-based estimation of above-ground biomass in heterogeneous arable fields: a comparative benchmark (2022, book chapter, Advances in Agricultural Remote Sensing: Methods and Applications (Springer)).
Authors: Milica Stanković (R0765); Uroš Marković (outside co-author); Claudia Reiter (outside co-author); Petra Varga (outside co-author).
Keywords: above-ground biomass; retrieval benchmark; radiative transfer; Sentinel-1; Gaussian process regression.
Above-ground biomass is a key variable for carbon accounting, crop insurance, and site-specific fertilisation, yet benchmark comparisons of retrieval methods across diverse sensor configurations are lacking for Pannonian agroecosystems. This book chapter presents a systematic comparison of six retrieval approaches—empirical vegetation index regression, radiative transfer model inversion, Gaussian process regression, random forest, gradient boosting, and a hybrid physical-statistical method—applied to estimating above-ground dry biomass in wheat, maize, and rapeseed fields in Vojvodina. Input data span Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery, Sentinel-1 radar backscatter, and airborne hyperspectral imaging, enabling assessment of sensor-specific advantages. Ground-truth biomass was measured destructively at 312 sampling points across two growing seasons. Results show that the hybrid physical-statistical approach consistently outperforms purely empirical methods, achieving an overall RMSE of 420 kg/ha and reducing bias under extreme biomass conditions. Sentinel-1 contributed most to accuracy for maize at late growth stages when optical saturation limits multispectral retrievals. The chapter concludes with practical guidelines for selecting retrieval methods depending on available sensor data, computational resources, and accuracy requirements in operational agricultural monitoring contexts.

SYN-PUB-08419.title: Towards operational yield gap assessment in Vojvodina using integrated Earth observation and crop simulation modelling
SYN-PUB-08419.text:
Towards operational yield gap assessment in Vojvodina using integrated Earth observation and crop simulation modelling (2020, journal, Field Crops Research).
Authors: Milica Stanković (R0765); Dragan Petković (outside co-author); Zoltán Fehér (outside co-author); Ivana Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: yield gap; data assimilation; ensemble Kalman filter; crop simulation; precision agriculture.
Yield gaps—the difference between attainable and actual farm yields—represent the primary target for sustainable intensification of agriculture. Quantifying yield gaps at parcel resolution across a large region requires combining the spatial detail of satellite Earth observation with the physiological realism of process-based crop models. This paper presents a framework that assimilates Sentinel-2 leaf area index retrievals into the APSERNA crop simulation model via an ensemble Kalman filter to generate spatially explicit attainable yield surfaces for winter wheat and maize across Vojvodina. Satellite-derived actual yields from a calibrated spectral reflectance model serve as the observed counterpart. The yield gap was estimated at 1.8 t/ha for maize and 1.2 t/ha for wheat on average, with marked spatial clustering: gaps were largest in fields with heavy clay soils and absent drainage infrastructure. Hotspot analysis identified 14 % of the agricultural area as high-priority zones where management improvements could close more than 60 % of the gap. Sensitivity analysis showed that nitrogen management and sowing date were the dominant controllable drivers. The framework is designed to interface directly with national agricultural advisory portals, providing actionable, field-level recommendations.

SYN-PUB-08420.title: Cloud-native processing architectures for continental-scale agricultural remote sensing: lessons from the Pannonian AgriCloud experiment
SYN-PUB-08420.text:
Cloud-native processing architectures for continental-scale agricultural remote sensing: lessons from the Pannonian AgriCloud experiment (2021, conference, Proceedings of the International Workshop on Cloud Platforms for Earth Observation).
Authors: Milica Stanković (R0765); Mihajlo Lazić (outside co-author); Andrej Kovač (outside co-author); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author).
Keywords: cloud-native; serverless; Sentinel; agricultural monitoring; scalability; Pannonian.
The shift from desktop-based to cloud-native processing is transforming operational agricultural remote sensing, yet published accounts of real-world deployment challenges for continental-scale workflows remain sparse. This conference paper reports lessons learned from the Pannonian AgriCloud experiment, in which a suite of Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 based agricultural monitoring products—covering crop type mapping, soil moisture, phenology, and yield forecasting—was deployed as a cloud-native service across a 200,000 km² domain spanning Serbia, Hungary, and Croatia. The architecture adopted a serverless function design with parallelised tile-level processing, an object storage backend, and a vector tile API for downstream client applications. End-to-end latency from Sentinel data availability to dashboard update was reduced from 48 hours in a prototype on-premise system to 4.2 hours in the cloud deployment. Bottlenecks were identified in the atmospheric correction step and in vector rendering of parcel-level outputs. Cost modelling showed that cloud processing became economically favourable over on-premise infrastructure at an annual processing volume exceeding 12,000 Sentinel-2 tiles. The paper discusses implications for national agricultural monitoring agencies and commercial precision agriculture service providers seeking scalable satellite analytics capacity.

SYN-PUB-10775.title: Procena referentne evapotranspiracije primenom metode FAO Penman-Monteith u uslovima ograničenih meteoroloških podataka u Vojvodini
SYN-PUB-10775.text:
Procena referentne evapotranspiracije primenom metode FAO Penman-Monteith u uslovima ograničenih meteoroloških podataka u Vojvodini (2013, journal, Vodoprivreda – časopis za vodnu privredu Srbije).
Authors: Milena Pantelić (R1047); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Branislav Kurjački (outside co-author).
Keywords: referentna evapotranspiracija; FAO Penman-Monteith; nedostajući meteorološki podaci; Vojvodina.
Metoda FAO Penman-Monteith (FAO-PM) smatra se standardnim pristupom za procenu referentne evapotranspiracije (ETo), ali zahteva niz meteoroloških ulaznih podataka koji u praksi često nisu dostupni. U radu je ispitana mogućnost zamene nedostajućih podataka o vlažnosti vazduha i brzini vetra vrednostima preuzetim iz regionalne klimatološke baze za period 2000–2011. na osam meteoroloških stanica u Vojvodini. Rezultati su upoređeni sa merenjima na lizimetarskoj stanici u Rimskim Šančevima. Utvrđeno je da zamena podataka o vlažnosti klimatološkim prosecima unosi grešku ETo od prosečno 4,1% na mesečnom nivou, dok zamena podataka o brzini vetra povećava grešku na 7,8%. Kombinovana zamena oba parametra daje ukupnu mesečnu grešku ispod 9%, što se ocenjuje prihvatljivim za potrebe operativnog zakazivanja navodnjavanja. Preporučuje se primena korekcijskih faktora izvedenih za svaku stanicu posebno.

SYN-PUB-10776.title: Modeliranje vodnog bilansa parcele soje primenom modela CROPWAT 8.0 i verifikacija na osnovu terenskih merenja vlažnosti zemljišta
SYN-PUB-10776.text:
Modeliranje vodnog bilansa parcele soje primenom modela CROPWAT 8.0 i verifikacija na osnovu terenskih merenja vlažnosti zemljišta (2017, conference, Zbornik radova, 48. savetovanje agronoma Srbije, Zlatibor).
Authors: Milena Pantelić (R1047); Nataša Moravčević (outside co-author).
Keywords: CROPWAT; soja; vodni bilans; FDR sonde; pedotransferne funkcije.
U radu je prikazana primena modela CROPWAT 8.0 za simulaciju dekadnog vodnog bilansa parcele soje (sorta NS Maximus) tokom vegetacijske sezone 2015. godine na području Bačke. Ulazni meteorološki podaci preuzeti su sa automatske stanice u Bečeju, a karakteristike zemljišta određene su laboratorijskim analizama uzoraka sa dubine do 90 cm. Simulirani sadržaj vode u zemljištu upoređen je sa FDR merenjima na četiri dubine u nedeljnim intervalima. Modelom je u proseku precenjen sadržaj vode za 6,4 mm u fazi vegetativnog porasta, što se pripisuje izostanku parametrizacije kapilarnog uspona u modelu. Primenom korekcije na osnovu pedotransfernih funkcija za glinasta ilovača tla, greška je smanjena na 3,1 mm. Zaključuje se da CROPWAT može biti pouzdan alat za operativno navodnjavnje u regionu uz adekvatno podešavanje parametara tla.

SYN-PUB-10777.title: Prostorna interpolacija referentne evapotranspiracije u Vojvodini korišćenjem kriging metode i digitalnog modela reljefa
SYN-PUB-10777.text:
Prostorna interpolacija referentne evapotranspiracije u Vojvodini korišćenjem kriging metode i digitalnog modela reljefa (2021, journal, Melioracije – naučno-stručni časopis za uređenje, korišćenje i zaštitu zemljišta i voda).
Authors: Stefan Varga (outside co-author); Daniela Horvat (outside co-author); Milena Pantelić (R1047).
Keywords: prostorna interpolacija; kriging; referentna evapotranspiracija; DEM; Vojvodina.
Referentna evapotranspiracija (ETo) procenjena metodom FAO-PM izračunata je na osnovu dnevnih podataka sa mreže od 12 meteoroloških stanica u Vojvodini za period 2010–2019. Na osnovu godišnjih suma ETo izvršena je prostorna interpolacija primenom obične kriging metode i kriging sa spoljašnjim trendom, gde je nadmorska visina iz digitalnog modela reljefa (SRTM, 30 m) korišćena kao pomoćna promenljiva. Unakrsna validacija pokazala je da kriging sa spoljašnjim trendom daje RMSE od 11,3 mm/godišnje ETo, u poređenju sa 18,7 mm kod obične kriging metode. Razlike u prostornoj raspodeli ETo unutar ravničarskog dela Vojvodine su relativno male (maksimalna amplituda 42 mm/god.), ali postaju značajne u pojasu Fruške Gore (razlika do 87 mm/god.), što ukazuje na potrebu za zasebnom parametrizacijom pri regionalnom planiranju navodnjavanja.

SYN-PUB-10778.title: Sensitivity of FAO-PM evapotranspiration estimates to systematic biases in input climate variables: a Monte Carlo approach applied to Pannonian lowland conditions
SYN-PUB-10778.text:
Sensitivity of FAO-PM evapotranspiration estimates to systematic biases in input climate variables: a Monte Carlo approach applied to Pannonian lowland conditions (2025, journal, Agricultural and Forest Meteorology).
Authors: Mirjam Vuković (outside co-author); Péter Kovács (outside co-author); Milena Pantelić (R1047); Daniela Horvat (outside co-author).
Keywords: FAO Penman-Monteith; sensitivity analysis; Monte Carlo; measurement uncertainty; Pannonian lowland.
Systematic measurement biases in temperature, humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation affect the accuracy of FAO Penman-Monteith evapotranspiration (ETo) calculations, but their relative importance under Pannonian lowland climate conditions has not been quantified comprehensively. A Monte Carlo framework was constructed in which each of the four input variables was independently perturbed with normally distributed errors parameterised from documented sensor calibration uncertainties. A total of 10,000 realisations were run for each of three representative months (April, July, October) using baseline data from Novi Sad station (2010–2022). Results indicate that ETo is most sensitive to air temperature biases in spring (a +1 °C bias causes a +3.8% change in monthly ETo), while wind speed biases dominate uncertainty in summer months (a +0.5 m/s bias causes +6.2%). Relative humidity biases contribute less than 2.5% across all months under the tested range. These findings support prioritisation of anemometer maintenance in operational agrometeorological networks used for irrigation advisory services.

SYN-PUB-10779.title: Procena efekta malčiranja na smanjenje evaporacije iz zemljišta i ukupnih potreba za navodnjavanjem paprike u uslovima Bačke
SYN-PUB-10779.text:
Procena efekta malčiranja na smanjenje evaporacije iz zemljišta i ukupnih potreba za navodnjavanjem paprike u uslovima Bačke (2026, journal, Acta Agriculturae Serbica).
Authors: Milena Pantelić (R1047); Đorđe Savić (outside co-author); Aleksandra Nišević (outside co-author).
Keywords: malčiranje; evaporacija; navodnjavanje paprike; FAO-56 dvofazni model; vodni bilans.
Terenski ogled sproveden je tokom dve vegetacijske sezone (2023. i 2024.) na Oglednom polju Rimski Šančevi s ciljem kvantifikacije uticaja polietilenskog malča na evaporaciju iz zemljišta i potrebe za navodnjavanjem paprike (Capsicum annuum L., sorta Zlatni medal). Postavljeno je šest tretmana u tri ponavljanja: crni PE malč, beli PE malč i kontrola (bez malča), uz dve norme navodnjavanja (puno i ograničeno – 70% ET). Evaporacija iz zemljišta procenjena je primenom jednačine FAO-56 dvofaznog modela, a vlažnost zemljišta praćena FDR sondama. U prvoj godini, crni malč smanjio je sezonu evaporacije za 41% u poređenju sa kontrolom; u drugoj godini efekat je iznosio 37%. Ukupna norma navodnjavanja pri punoj ET bila je manja za 58 mm (crni malč) i 41 mm (beli malč) u odnosu na kontrolu. Prinos paprike u tretmanu crni malč–puna ET bio je za 12% viši od kontrole.

W2896715775.title: Dynamic Neural Network Modelling of Soil Moisture Content for Predictive Irrigation Scheduling
W2896715775.text: Sensors, 2018. Sustainable freshwater management is underpinned by technologies which improve the efficiency of agricultural irrigation systems. Irrigation scheduling has the potential to incorporate real-time feedback from soil moisture and climatic sensors. However, for robust closed-loop decision support, models of the soil moisture dynamics are essential in order to predict crop water needs while adapting to external perturbation and disturbances. This paper presents a Dynamic Neural Network approach for modelling of the temporal soil moisture fluxes. The models are trained to generate a one-day-ahead prediction of the volumetric soil moisture content based on past soil moisture, precipitation, and climatic measurements. Using field data from three sites, a R 2 value above 0.94 was obtained during model evaluation in all sites. The models were also able to generate robust soil moisture predictions for independent sites which were not used in training the models. The application of the Dynamic Neural Network models in a predictive irrigation scheduling system was demonstrated using AQUACROP simulations of the potato-growing season. The predictive irrigation scheduling system was evaluated against a rule-based system that applies irrigation based on predefined thresholds. Results indicate that the predictive system achieves a water saving ranging between 20 and 46% while realizing a yield and water use efficiency similar to that of the rule-based system.

W2924508481.title: Irrigation Factor Approach Based on Soil Water Content: A Nectarine Orchard Case Study
W2924508481.text: Water, 2019. Precision agriculture requires irrigation supported by an accurate knowledge of the crop water requirements. In this paper, a novel approach for drip irrigation scheduling of fruit trees is presented based on the results obtained during a full growing season in an early-maturing nectarine orchard growing in a clay loam soil in a Mediterranean environment. Real-time water content was monitored in the soil profile of the main root exploration zone by means of capacitance probes; in addition, plant water status (midday stem water potential and leaf gas exchange) and canopy development were frequently measured throughout the vegetative cycle. The reference evapotranspiration (ET0) values, taken from a nearby automatic meteorological station, and the measured irrigation values allowed the determination of the irrigation factors once irrigation drainage during the season was assumed to be negligible and plant water status was proved to be adequate. The proposed irrigation factors offer a hands-on approach as an easy tool for irrigation management based on suitable soil water deficits, allowing the water requirements of nectarine trees under precision irrigation to be determined in semi-arid agrosystems where water resources are limited.
